case_name: Manoj and others v State of Haryana
respondent:
State of Haryana
Supreme Court of India

9 July 2013
Cr.A. No. 1853 of 2012
The Judgment was delivered by : Sudhansu Jyoti Mukhopadhaya, J.
1. The appellants in this case were found guilty of offence punishable under Sections 498-A and 304-B Indian Penal Code (for short, "IPC") by the Sessions Judge, Bhiwani. They were sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life for the offence under Section 304-B IPC and also to undergo rigorous imprisonment for three years, besides, payment of fine of Rs.5,000/- each and in default of which to undergo further imprisonment for a period of six months for the offence under Section 498-A IPC. Their appeal against the said judgment and conviction to the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh got dismissed except with a modification in the sentence of imprisonment from imprisonment for life to imprisonment for 10 years for the offence under Section 304-B IPC.

facts: The appellants were found guilty of offence punishable under Sections 498-A and 304-B Indian Penal Code (IPC) by the Sessions Judge, Bhiwani.
On 14.4.2005, Meena Devi, wife of Manoj Kumar, was admitted to Government Hospital, Bhiwani with burn injuries.

The prosecution case is that on account of greed of dowry, Meena Devi was set on fire by pouring kerosene oil on her by her husband Manoj, mother-in-law Chameli Devi and husband's elder brother's wife Suman after colluding with each other.
All together eleven witnesses were produced by the prosecution in support of their case.
Exhibits were proved through the prosecution witnesses.
issues: Whether the dying declaration recorded by Dr. Rajinder Rai (PW-4) is reliable?
Whether the accused persons should be convicted under Section 302 IPC instead of Section 304-B IPC?
petitioner_arguments: The dying declaration recorded by Dr. Rajinder Rai (PW-4) is not reliable.
The trial Court and High Court erred in convicting the accused persons under Section 304-B IPC instead of Section 302 IPC.
respondent_arguments: The dying declaration recorded by Dr. Rajinder Rai (PW-4) is trustworthy, cogent and reliable.
The prosecution has miserably failed to prove its case against all the four accused for the offence u/ss. 302 and 406 r/w S. 34 IPC.
court_reasoning: The Court held that the dying declaration recorded by Dr. Rajinder Rai (PW-4) is reliable and trustworthy.
The Court affirmed the conviction of the accused persons under Section 304-B IPC.
holding: The appeal preferred by the appellants against the judgment passed by the Sessions Judge, Bhiwani was dismissed.
The modification in the sentence of imprisonment from imprisonment for life to imprisonment for 10 years for the offence under Section 304-B IPC was affirmed.
